newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - U.S. technology trade publications.

text.p: For the weeks of Jan. 6, here are some of the top stories reported in major U.S. technology trade publications.

PC WEEK - AT&T Corp later this month will kick off a version of its WorldNet Internet service that runs with cable modems, giving users T-1 accesss speeds at costs closer to ISDN digital telephone service, PC Week reported Jan. 6.

IBM Corp, MasterCard Intl and RSA Data Security will be among a cadre of technology vendors to jolt Internet commerce with applications and systems based on the first version of the Secure Electronic Transaction specification later this month, PC Week reported Jan. 6.

COMPUTERWORLD - The vast task of converting corporate computer systems to fix Year 2000 software is spurring a variety of entrepreneurial efforts designed to slash the cost of year 2000 code conversion work, Computerworld reported January 6. Efforts include a regional effort by Omaha, Neb. businesses to train teachers, retail clerks and other non-technical workers to become low-cost Cobol programmers.

A new report commissioned by the U.S. Defense of Department recommends the agency spend an additional $3 billion over the next five years to beef up the nation's computer systems against terrorists and individual hacker attacks, Computerworld also reported.

COMMUNICATIONS WEEK - MCI Communications Corp has begun activating the first leg of an ultra-high speed network that allows it to transmit voice and data at up to 40 gigabits per second, or four times the speed of its existing high-speed network based on Synchronous Optical Network technology, Communications Week reported January 6. MCI is using a new hybrid transmission method to connect Chicago and St. Louis.

Communications Week also predicted that network managers will become less obsessed with introducing new networking technologies during 1997 and focus increasingly on deploying practical applications that take fuller advantage of the existing wide area network infrastructure.

COMPUTER RESELLER NEWS - Apple Computer Inc's chairman and CEO is expected to detail its revised operating system plans on Tuesday, the first details of how Apple plans to integrate its planned purchase of Next Software and how the Next technology will help solve Apple's delays in brining the next version of the Mac OS to the market, CRN reported Jan. 6.

International Business Machines Corp plans to hire about 15,000 new service employees this year and will recruit professionals from other companies to fill the lion's share of those slots, CRN reported Jan. 6.

MACWEEK - Two and a half weeks after the news, Apple's acquisition of Next Software has left company executives scrambling for explanations and the scant details on how it will merge the technologies and how they will provide compatibility with current Mac software have left software developers and users nonplused, MacWeek reported Jan. 6.

The Mac community is avidly awaiting a taste of Apple's Next strategy at this week's MacWorld show. In the meantime, a trove of hardware and software offerings will represent the current state of the Mac, including a celebration of its 20th anniversary with a limited edition Mac to ship this summer.

INFOWORLD - Sweeping changes are coming to the desktop this year, with Microsoft Corp preparing to send out beta versions of its next OS, code-named Memphis, this quarter with a final version due in the third quarter, Infoworld reported Jan. 6.

While the multimedia extensions of Intel's PentiumPro chip will be available in the first half of 1997, systems built around the processors are likely to be expensive and will initially lack some highly touted technologies, such as high speed synchronous DRAM (SDRAM), Infoworld reported Jan. 6.

INFORMATION WEEK - This could be a make it or break it year for Sybase Inc, as the software company hopes to escape the financial doldrums and regain customer confidence with new products and an aggressive strategy, Information Week reported Jan. 6.

Microsoft quietly began the new year by beginning early testing of the next major release of Windows 95, but the code still lacks an integrated Internet browser and management functions, Information Week reported Jan. 6.

EE TIMES - A report by a federally funded networking research group suggests that severe Internet congestion might be linked to "routing instability," where the heavy traffic emanating from routers bogs down the public network, EE Times reported Jan. 6. Researchers suggest that routers made by Cisco Systems Inc have inherent router flaws that may exacerbate the problem, EE Times said.

The established vendors of personal computer graphics chips may have to fight for their lives this year as semiconductor-industry giants, including Intel Corp, Philips Components and SGS-Thomson Microelectronics, storm the market, EE Times reported Jan. 6.

ELECTRONIC BUYERS' NEWS - The Korean Semiconductor Association has offered to follow the system of calculating integrated circuit production that has been been adopted by the Japanese and U.S. chip industries. But in exchange, the U.S.would have to drop a long-simmering DRAM dumping case against Hyundai Electronics Industries Co Ltd and LG Electronics Inc, EBN reported Jan. 6.

LSI Logic Corp is finding itself positioned to become the leading supplier of standard products for the next wave of consumer electronics applications, such as DVD players, digital cameras, set-top boxes, EBN reported Jan. 6.

COMPUTER RETAIL WEEK - With several retail chains reporting third quarter losses and others poised to close stores, the industry faces a drastically changed landscape in 1997, Computer Retail Week reported Jan. 6.

Intel Corp is snapping the industry to push its newest Pentium processor, with its January 8 launch of its MMX technology, but it won't be easy given 1996's difficult fourth quarter, retailers and vendors said, CRW reported Jan. 6.
